title: Ascot Wealth Management Review 2026: Legit or Scam?
description: Ascot Wealth Management review: an FCA-regulated adviser with no minimum assets, a free first call, 0.5% to 1% yearly fees and conflicting firm history.
author: James Whitmore
excerpt: Ascot Wealth Management says it is FCA regulated and charges 0.5% to 1% a year, but its founding date and client figures do not match across its site.
content:
Ascot Wealth Management is a UK financial adviser that presents itself as based in Ascot. It offers investment management, retirement, protection, mortgage and financial planning advice. It is not an AI trading tool, so this review checks it as an adviser.

The firm says it is FCA regulated and offers a free first call. This review sets out what its website says, where its own figures differ, and what to check before you share financial details.

Ascot Wealth Management at a Glance

The table summarises what the firm's website states. Figures that conflict across the site are covered in the sections below.

CategoryWhat the page says
Service typeFinancial advice: investment management, retirement, protection, mortgage and financial planning, and corporate services
RegulationSays it is fully authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, and points visitors to the FCA Register
Minimum assetsNo strict minimum stated
First contactFree 20-minute phone call, then a free discovery meeting if the fit is right
FeesOne-off fee for initial advice; fixed fee for advice and implementation; ongoing management typically 0.5% to 1% a year
Client moneyHeld with custodian platforms, separate from the firm's business assets; FSCS protection up to £85,000 per eligible person per firm
OfficeScotch Corner, London Road, Sunningdale, Berkshire SL5 0ER
TeamFounder and director Mark Insley, with wealth managers listed on the site

Items come from the firm's website as published when we reviewed it. We have not contacted the firm.

Is Ascot Wealth Management Legit? What the Claims Show

The site makes broad claims about trust. It says the firm puts clients first, gives straight answers and does not chase commission. It also shows a 4.8/5 average from 1,195 verified reviews and a figure of £500M+ in assets under management.

Service model

Advice comes from a named adviser after a discovery meeting. The site describes one dedicated adviser who knows the client's full financial picture, with plans set out in plain English and options explained before any work starts.

Track record and ratings

The site shows a 4.8/5 average from 1,195 verified reviews and ratings for four advisers. Its counters show £0M+ in assets and a 0.0 client rating in the text we read, while other sections claim £500M+. The founding date is given as 2010, but other sections say the firm has been in Ascot for over 30 years.

What the firm covers

The firm lists investment management, retirement planning, protection planning, mortgage advisory, financial planning and corporate services. The site gives no detail on how the mortgage and corporate work are charged.

Costs Worth Knowing

The site says the initial consultation is free and that advice and implementation carry a fixed fee agreed upfront. Ongoing management is typically 0.5% to 1% a year, and the firm says it will explain all costs in writing before any work begins. It gives no pound figure for the fixed fee.

Who Is Behind the Brand

The firm is described as fully authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, and the site refers visitors to the FCA Register to check it. It names a founder and director, Mark Insley. Its office is in Sunningdale, Berkshire, although the firm presents itself as based in Ascot.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Check the firm and each adviser on the FCA Register before you share financial details.
  • Ask for the fixed advice fee and the ongoing percentage in writing before the first meeting.
  • Ask which founding date is correct, since the site gives both 2010 and over 30 years in Ascot.
  • Ask how your investments are held and confirm which FSCS protection applies to your situation.

Risks to Keep in Mind

The site says the firm does not push products or chase commission. In the text we read, it does not say that investments can fall in value or that a plan may fail to meet its goals. Those are the points most worth confirming in the first meeting.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a minimum amount to invest?

The site says there are no strict minimum asset requirements. It asks prospective clients to book a free consultation to discuss their situation.

Is Ascot Wealth Management regulated?

The site says it is fully authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. Check its entry on the FCA Register yourself.

Where is my money held?

The site says investments are held with FCA-regulated custodian platforms, separate from the firm's business assets, and that FSCS protection applies up to £85,000 per eligible person per firm.

How much does it cost?

The initial consultation is free. Advice and implementation carry a fixed fee agreed upfront, and ongoing management is typically 0.5% to 1% a year.

Our Verdict on Ascot Wealth Management

Ascot Wealth Management presents as an FCA-regulated adviser with clear fee bands and a free first call. Its own figures for its founding date and client numbers do not agree, and the site gives no fixed fee amounts. Our rating reflects what we could and could not confirm.
